correctness.rationale: Trace-one scaling x=tz with t in k× makes the map t³ N(z). Cube roots are counted exactly by cubic characters. Odd-characteristic trace-one norm counting gives 1-χ(1-4n), and the Jacobi–Gauss identity implies |S|²=q; characteristic-two norm counting gives 1-ψ(n), and an additive Gauss sum again implies |S|²=q. Cubic orthogonality yields exactly 2q(q-1) squared deviation. q>4 gives q-2√q>0; q=4 trace-one norms are ω,ω² and the only missing target is 1. A standalone exact field enumerator verifies q=2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11,13,16 (794 inputs). The infinite proof does not rely on enumeration.

value.rationale: Trace times norm is a canonical cubic invariant of quadratic field extensions. The exact all-prime-power preimage law, sharp cubic-residue phase transition, nonzero-target variance 2q(q-1), and unique four-element-base-field failure of surjectivity give a natural full arithmetic classification, not an arbitrary small sample, generic degree bound or table recomputation. The explicit cubically twisted character sum is the natural exact invariant when the fibers are nonuniform.
